title.official: Agreement on the Establishment of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization

issuer.name: Founding States of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization
Government of the People's Republic of China

relevance.reason: The constituent treaty of the first intergovernmental international organization specifically dedicated to artificial intelligence. It establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental organization with international legal personality, headquartered in Shanghai, with a Council and a Secretariat, and limits its functions exclusively to the civilian domain of AI (Article 3(2)). It is subject to ratification, acceptance or approval and enters into force on the deposit of the third such instrument (Article 15). It is a treaty, not a political declaration, and it is the second AI-specific treaty in the corpus alongside CETS 225.
ai_provisions: Article 1 — establishes WAICO as an independent intergovernmental international organization with international legal personality
Article 2 — purposes: human-centric AI, international cooperation, bridging the AI divide, risk mitigation and trustworthy AI

Article 3 — functions, including capacity building, alignment of governance rules and technical standards, open-source cooperation and support for the UN framework; functions are limited exclusively to the civilian domain
Article 4 — principles: UN Charter, sovereignty, diversity of civilizations, equality, multilateralism and extensive consultation
Articles 5–8 — Council, decision-making, Secretariat and financing
Article 10 — membership open to all States; Founding Members are States that sign during the open-for-signature period
Article 14 — signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026; ratification, acceptance or approval; accession thereafter
Article 15 — entry into force on the third instrument of ratification, acceptance or approval
Article 18 — China as depositary; Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts equally authentic
relevance.excluded_scope: Military AI is excluded: Article 3(2) limits the Organization's functions exclusively to the civilian domain. The Agreement establishes an organization and a cooperation framework; it does not itself set product rules, prohibitions, testing standards or a judicial dispute-settlement mechanism. Disputes are to be settled by consultation (Article 13).

dates.notes: Signed at the Shanghai ceremony on 16 July 2026. The Agreement was open for signature from 1 May to 31 July 2026. China's National People's Congress Standing Committee approved ratification on 6 November 2026; the deposit of the instrument of ratification and any depositary notification of entry into force were not verified.

status_note: Treaty, binding on States that become parties, but not in force as of 23 November 2026. Article 15 requires three instruments of ratification, acceptance or approval for entry into force. China's National People's Congress approved ratification on 6 November 2026; no depositary register or notification of a deposited ratification was located, so the record does not count a ratification and the map records signature only. China's MFA reports 38 founding members, but the primary signing records individually identify 37: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight additional States on 30–31 July 2026. The 38th member is not named in the primary record; the discrepancy is recorded, not resolved.

parties.summary: 38 founding members reported by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; 37 individually identified in the signing records: 29 States at the 16 July 2026 ceremony and eight additional States on 30–31 July 2026. China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026, but no deposit was verified. The identity of the 38th reported founding member is not stated in the official sources located.

notes: Approved by the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress on 6 November 2026.
Deposit of the instrument of ratification was not verified; no ratification is counted.

unknowns: The MFA reports 38 founding members as of 9 November 2026, but the signing records individually identify 37. The 38th member is not named in the MFA statements, the October 2026 MFA progress report or the Indonesian government's list of the 29 initial signatories.

No depositary register or notification of signatures, ratifications or entry into force was located. The count of deposited ratifications is therefore 0, notwithstanding China's national approval on 6 November 2026.
The Agreement remains open to accession after 31 July 2026 (Article 14(3)); later accessions are not Founding Members and are not included in this list.
The exact date on which the MFA's 38-country count was reached is not stated; the October 2026 progress report already gives 38.

languages.note: Article 18: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish texts are equally authentic. Only the English reproduction of the Agreement was read; no official deposited text was acquired.

States that WAICO is an independent intergovernmental international organization headquartered in Shanghai, that the Agreement follows the purposes of the UN Charter, and that representatives of 29 countries signed and became founding members.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China

related.note: China's 2023 Global AI Governance Initiative is the policy line that led to the proposal for WAICO; it is a unilateral non-binding document, whereas the WAICO Agreement is a treaty.
The other AI-specific treaty in the corpus. CETS 225 is a human-rights framework convention; WAICO is a constituent instrument of an intergovernmental organization. Neither is in force.
The US-led Pax Silica coalition is the counterpart architecture. Kazakhstan is a signatory of both the Pax Silica Declaration and the WAICO Agreement.

gaps: The Agreement is not in force: Article 15 requires three deposited ratifications, acceptances or approvals, and none was verified.
China's NPC approved ratification on 6 November 2026, but the deposit of the instrument and any depositary notification were not verified; no ratification is counted.
The MFA reports 38 founding members while the signing records individually identify 37; the 38th member is not named in the official sources located.
No depositary register or status table for signatures, ratifications and accessions was located.
The full official text was not acquired; the record is metadata-only and relies on a reproduction for the article analysis.
The Organization's functions are limited to the civilian domain; military AI is outside the Agreement.
The Council, Secretariat, rules of procedure, budget and implementing instruments do not yet exist or were not verified.
